summary.text: Cassini–Huygens was a joint mission by NASA, the European Space Agency and the Italian Space Agency to study Saturn and its system, including its rings and moons.
It had two craft: NASA's Cassini probe, the first to enter Saturn's orbit, and ESA's Huygens lander, which landed on Titan.
It ended on September 15, 2017, when Cassini burned up in Saturn's atmosphere so that it could not contaminate moons that might offer habitable environments.

facts.label: Partners
facts.value: NASA, ESA and the Italian Space Agency

items.prompt: After Huygens landed on Titan, how did its data get back to Earth?

options.label: It passed through the Cassini orbiter, which acted as a relay
It beamed straight to antennas on Earth
A network of satellites around Titan relayed it
It was stored aboard and carried home later

items.explain: Huygens returned data to Earth for around 90 minutes, using the orbiter as a relay.

items.prompt: Why was Cassini deliberately sent into Saturn at the end of the mission?

options.label: Its instruments had worn out and could not be repaired
To avoid any risk of contaminating moons that might be habitable
To collect samples from deep inside Saturn's atmosphere
Its orbit had drifted too far to be corrected

items.explain: Cassini burned up to prevent any risk of contaminating Saturn's moons, which might have offered habitable environments to stowaway microbes.

items.prompt: To meet budget limits, planners cut one thing from Cassini to save $250 million. What was it?

options.label: The Huygens lander
The main radio antenna
The scan platform
The infrared instrument

items.explain: To comply with budget restrictions, Cassini was downsized and the scan platform was removed from the plans.

items.prompt: The Huygens lander was named for an astronomer and mathematician. What did he discover?

options.label: Titan
The divisions in Saturn's rings
Four of Saturn's other satellites
Saturn itself

items.explain: Christiaan Huygens discovered Titan. Giovanni Cassini was the one who discovered the ring divisions and four satellites.

items.prompt: Cassini was first scheduled for four years of work at Saturn, yet stayed 13 years. How did that happen?

options.label: Its original plan was a minimum, so it just kept going
Italy's space agency took over with a second spacecraft
Huygens carried on once Cassini ran out of fuel
NASA extended the mission twice, first as Equinox and then as Solstice

items.explain: The mission was extended once as the Cassini Equinox Mission and a second time as the Cassini Solstice Mission.

items.prompt: How did Huygens get down to the surface of Titan?

options.label: It floated down on a parachute after separating from Cassini
It fired landing rockets after separating from Cassini
It was lowered on a cable from Cassini
It rolled down from Cassini on wheels

items.explain: Huygens separated from Cassini and landed by parachute on Titan.
